Average Shortest Path Centrality

Source: R/centrality-batch66.R
centrality_asp_centrality.Rd

Average shortest path centrality (AC; Lv et al. 2019) is the relative growth of the average distance of a network when the ties of a node are removed: $$AC(k) = \frac{|ASP(G'_k) - ASP(G)|}{ASP(G)}, \qquad ASP(G) = \frac{1}{N(N - 1)} \sum_{i \ne j} d_{ij},$$ where \(G'_k\) is the network without the ties of node \(k\), and a pair that cannot reach each other counts the diameter of the original network.

Usage

centrality_asp_centrality(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Network input accepted by centrality.

...

Further arguments to centrality, such as normalized.

Value

A named numeric vector with one score per node, in input node order.

Details

The measure is computed on the simple undirected skeleton of the network, so direction, weights, loops and parallel edges are ignored. Node \(k\) stays in \(G'_k\) as an isolated node, so its own pairs count the diameter and \(N(N - 1)\) does not change: the source's worked example computes it so, and its printed numbers, nine scores and two averages, follow this reading and not the \(N - 1\) nodes its prose describes. The score is therefore never negative. On a disconnected network the unreachable pairs of the network itself also count its largest finite distance. An edgeless network and a one-node network score 0. On a connected network without cut vertices the score is a decreasing linear function of centrality_closeness_vitality, so the two rank nodes in exactly opposite order; they differ at cut vertices, where the pairs that are cut off count the diameter. The score ranks nodes almost like centrality_exogenous (Kendall correlation 0.997 on the karate club network, 0.94 to 0.95 on three random networks). The implementation reproduces the nine scores the source prints for its 9-node example, on the edge list read from its figure. The distances are computed again for each node, so the cost is that of the distances times the number of nodes. normalized = TRUE divides the scores by their maximum.

References

Lv, Z., Zhao, N., Xiong, F. and Chen, N. (2019). A novel measure of identifying influential nodes in complex networks. Physica A: Statistical Mechanics and its Applications, 523, 488-497. doi:10.1016/j.physa.2019.01.136 .

See also

centrality_closeness_vitality, centrality_exogenous, centrality_average_distance, centrality.

Examples

centrality_asp_centrality(regulation_net)
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#> 0.07936508 0.09523810 0.11111111 0.09523810 0.07936508 0.07936508 0.06349206 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#> 0.07936508 0.09523810 0.07936508
